key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants like Ca can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and modifying vacancy chemistry.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical materials-design lever for proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cells, potentially reducing CO2/SO2 degradation while maintaining or improving conductivity.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site electronegativity and ionic radius effects
Evaluation of proton transport, vacancy formation, and gas adsorption trends
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational evidence that Ca doping enhances oxygen-vacancy formation, proton uptake, suppresses impurity phases, and weakens adsorption of acidic gases such as CO2 and SO2.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on whether proton transfer is the rate-limiting step, and Ca surface segregation could alter grain-boundary behavior in real devices.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
